% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-10-09
MIXED ROTATIONCyclicals +0.6% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

Tech is running alone and everything else is paying for it. XLK gained 8.83% over the past month while all ten other sectors fell, with XLB down 7.72%, XLF down 7.23%, and XLRE down 6.68%. Year to date, XLK sits at 38.47% and XLE at 37.61%, which tells you this is a two-engine market where one engine has now stalled. The theme tables sharpen the same point. Cyber gained 24.5% in a month, semis 17.3%, AI infrastructure 15.5%, and software 8.3%. Every other theme you own lost money, with GLP-1 down 16.2%, uranium down 15.1%, gold miners down 9.7%, and banks down 8.6%. Rotation right now means concentration, not broadening.

You're paying for this in the defensive complex. XLRE fell 6.68% on the month and sits at a -3.18 z-score on its ratio to SPY, in the bottom 1% of its yearly range. Utilities fell 6.66% and the XLU/SPY ratio is at -2.30, in the bottom 2% of its yearly range. The XLY and XLP 1-month returns of -4.20% and -5.85% tell the same story. This is not a classic risk-on tape. It's a narrow tape where capital is fleeing anything that isn't AI-adjacent, and the sectors that normally catch a rotation bid are getting sold instead.

The most stretched ratios say the market has picked a lane and is flooring the accelerator. XLK/XLU is at a 2.55 z-score and in the top 1% of its yearly range, with a year-to-date move of 50.1%. QQQ/TLT is at 2.38 and SPY/TLT at 2.33, both in the top 1% of their yearly range, which means you're being paid to own equities over duration in the most crowded way in a year. The anti-cyclical pair is just as extreme: IWM/QQQ is at -2.47 and SIZE/SPY at -2.61, with SIZE/SPY in the bottom 1% of its yearly range. Small caps are being abandoned while mega-cap tech extends. The tension is this: cyclical leadership without economic breadth. Either the small-cap and defensive ratios mean-revert, or the tech bid is the only game in town and everything else keeps bleeding. You should be sizing for the second outcome until XLK/XLU rolls over.

Tech extraordinance versus broad-market erosion: XLK up 8.83% while every other sector is negative on the month

BULL

AI-linked leadership is intact, with cyber up 24.5%, semis up 17.3%, AI infrastructure up 15.5%, and XLK/XLU at a 2.55 z-score in the top 1% of its yearly range. That trend is confirmed, not exhausted.

BEAR

Breadth is deteriorating badly: IWM/QQQ at a -2.47 z-score and SIZE/SPY at -2.61 in the bottom 1% of its yearly range, while banks, gold miners, and GLP-1 all fell more than 8% on the month. The risk-on label doesn't apply to most stocks.

TELL

XLK/XLU holding above a 2.55 z-score while IWM/QQQ stays below -2.47 would confirm the narrow trend; any snapback in XLU or small-cap breadth would signal rotation is broadening.

⚠ Themes like cyber (**24.5%**) and AI infrastructure (**15.5%**) are in a confirmed, extended uptrend with XLK/XLU at a **2.55** z-score in the top 1% of its yearly range. vs Small-cap and equal-weight ratios are at extreme lows: IWM/QQQ at **-2.47** and SIZE/SPY at **-2.61**, both in the bottom 1% of their yearly ranges.: Conflicting readings of the same tape: one says the momentum bid is intact and narrow, the other says the broad market is being abandoned and may force a rotation. Trust the momentum reading while the credit ratios stay at their highs, because IWM/QQQ and SIZE/SPY have been in the bottom 1% of their yearly ranges for months without snapping back.
⚠ XLE is up **37.61%** year to date, a cyclical sector with a strong longer-term trend. vs XLE is down **3.50%** on the month, while XLK gained **8.83%** and XLK/XLU sits at a **2.55** z-score in the top 1% of its yearly range.: Energy's longer-term cyclical strength is being sold in favor of tech on the month, which means the cyclical leadership label is stale. Trust the monthly move because it's the live signal, and XLE/SPY is not on the stretched list even though XLE's yearly return is strong.

The ratios at absolute z-scores of 2.3 or higher are mostly trend confirmations, not mean-reversion setups. BKLN/HYG at 3.35 and SHY/TLT at 3.19 both sit in the top 1% of their yearly ranges and reflect a persistent credit-risk-on bid that has been in place all year.

AGG/TLT at 2.83, JNK/TLT at 2.47, and MBB/TLT at 2.34 tell the same story: money keeps flowing toward credit and short duration over long Treasuries. The mean-reversion candidates are on the equity side.

XLRE/SPY at -3.18 and XLU/SPY at -2.30 are both in the bottom 2% of their yearly ranges. IWM/QQQ at -2.47 and SIZE/SPY at -2.61 are in the bottom 1% of theirs.

These are the four ratios to watch if you're hunting for a rotation trade. XLK/XLU at 2.55, XLK/XLP at 2.30, and QQQ/TLT at 2.38 are extended but confirmed, and fighting them has been expensive since January.

The tell is whether the credit ratios start to roll while the defensive ratios stay pinned. If BKLN/HYG and SHY/TLT both retreat from their 3.35 and 3.19 extremes, that's when the small-cap and real-estate ratios are most likely to snap back.
